scope: Directed primary-source search on geometric and sparse graph attention, multilayer topology, learned attention supports and HU/MHU neural prior art. Not a systematic review or novelty certification.
search_queries: GraphGPS General Powerful Scalable Graph Transformer NeurIPS 2022 paper
Exphormer Sparse Transformers for Graphs ICML 2023
hyperuniform attention transformer neural network mask
site.proceedings.neurips.cc Graphormer Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation
site.proceedings.neurips.cc Big Bird Transformers Longer Sequences
site.proceedings.neurips.cc "Unifying and Enhancing Graph Transformers via a Hierarchical Mask Framework"

novelty_assessment.limitation: No equivalent evaluation was located in these directed searches; this is not evidence of absence, patentability, freedom to operate, or absolute originality. No legal opinion is provided.

sources.citation: Rampasek, L., Galkin, M., Dwivedi, V. P., Luu, A. T., Wolf, G., and Beaini, D. (2022). Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer. NeurIPS 35.
sources.verification: Official NeurIPS 2022 abstract and author list opened; publication status verified.
claims_supported: GraphGPS combines positional/structural encodings, local message passing and global attention.
Graph attention plus local processing is established prior art.
limitations: Reported graph benchmark performance does not establish a benefit from HU or MHU.
Linear complexity depends on the selected modules and should not be attributed to every full-attention instantiation.
sources.implementation_relevance: Use a modular local/attention decomposition for later architecture comparisons; hold it constant across geometry arms.

sources.citation: Shirzad, H., Velingker, A., Venkatachalam, B., Sutherland, D. J., and Sinop, A. K. (2023). Exphormer: Sparse Transformers for Graphs. ICML, PMLR 202:31613-31632.
sources.verification: Official ICML/PMLR abstract, bibliography and linked primary manuscript verified.
claims_supported: Exphormer uses sparse attention with expander graphs and virtual global nodes.
Sparse global communication is a strong rival to purely local geometric connectivity.
limitations: The construction has global communication resources absent from the historical LARP core.
Theoretical properties depend on the specified construction; a degree-budget adaptation is not automatically Exphormer.
sources.implementation_relevance: Include an expander rival and count every local, expander and global attention connection.

sources.citation: Zaheer, M., Guruganesh, G., Dubey, K. A., et al. (2020). Big Bird: Transformers for Longer Sequences. NeurIPS 33.
sources.verification: Official NeurIPS record and full-text sparse-graph definition inspected, including local/random/global patterns and conditional theoretical results.
claims_supported: BigBird combines local windows, random attention and global tokens.
A sparse support does not by itself imply that any particular geometric mask inherits the same expressivity properties.
limitations: The paper studies sequences and its specified patterns, not MHU-marked spatial computation.
Global tokens add communication and storage; compare their actual budget.
sources.implementation_relevance: Motivates a local-plus-shortcut rival and explicit accounting of attention pairs.

sources.citation: Ying, C., Cai, T., Luo, S., et al. (2021). Do Transformers Really Perform Badly for Graph Representation? NeurIPS 34.
sources.verification: Official abstract and full text inspected; degree centrality and shortest-path attention biases verified. Title on manuscript uses 'Bad' while official abstract uses 'Badly'.
claims_supported: Graphormer adds degree and shortest-path structural information to standard attention.
Geometry/structure encoded into dense attention is distinct from restricting its support.
limitations: Shortest-path graph structure is not the point-pattern structure factor.
Graph-level benchmark success does not establish functional multihyperuniformity.
sources.implementation_relevance: Compare geometric encodings against their ablations while separately controlling attention support.

sources.citation: Zhao, H., Jiang, L., Jia, J., Torr, P. H. S., and Koltun, V. (2021). Point Transformer. ICCV:16259-16268.
sources.verification: CVF search result supplies the accepted-version notice and exact ICCV bibliography; arXiv author record opened. Direct CVF opens returned internal errors, so no unverified fine-grained implementation claims are used in the report.
claims_supported: Point Transformer develops self-attention for point-cloud processing.
limitations: Input point clouds are not a certified MHU computational substrate.
Geometric attention is prior art independent of MHU.
sources.implementation_relevance: Provides a geometry-aware attention precedent without suggesting that MHU placement itself is novel or useful.

sources.citation: Shirzad, H., Lin, H., Venkatachalam, B., Velingker, A., Woodruff, D. P., and Sutherland, D. J. (2024). Even Sparser Graph Transformers. NeurIPS 37.
sources.verification: Official NeurIPS abstract opened and primary full-text search extracts inspected; two-stage layer-wise sparsification and publication venue verified.
claims_supported: Spexphormer uses a narrow trained model to select useful attention connections before training a larger model.
Task-dependent learned sparse topology is an existing alternative to fixed geometry.
limitations: Topology selection requires training and must be charged to the total budget.
It does not test HU or the distribution of distinct functional marks.
sources.implementation_relevance: A later learned-mask rival should include both training stages and selection opportunities in its cost/HPO ledger.

sources.citation: Xing, Y., Wang, X., Wu, B., Huang, H., and Shi, C. (2025). Unifying and Enhancing Graph Transformers via a Hierarchical Mask Framework. NeurIPS 38.
sources.verification: Official NeurIPS 2025 abstract, title, authors and DOI verified in primary conference record.
claims_supported: M3Dphormer combines hierarchical masks and mixture-of-experts routing.
Multiple masked interaction levels are close architectural prior art for multilayer/head proposals.
limitations: Classification label consistency assumptions should not be transferred to algorithmic tasks or used to select supports from targets.
The reported model does not identify any MHU effect.
sources.implementation_relevance: Supports separating mask construction from node/head parametrization and avoiding labels or targets in mask admission.

sources.citation: De Schouwer, J., Saez de Ocariz Borde, H., and Dong, X. (2026). k-Maximum Inner Product Attention for Graph Transformers and the Expressive Power of GraphGPS. GRaM workshop, PMLR 326:145-183.
sources.verification: Official PMLR bibliographic record, workshop venue and abstract inspected; main-conference status is not claimed and review process was not independently audited.
claims_supported: k-MIP selects relevant key nodes per query by a top-k inner-product operation.
Content-dependent sparse attention is a current alternative to fixed geometry-derived support.
limitations: Conditional approximation statements are not guarantees for LARP's finite width, depth or degree.
Sparse output support does not make neighbor search free; charge selection cost.
sources.implementation_relevance: Consider only after a fixed-mask diagnostic, with complete selection and training costs.

sources.citation: Martelli, F., Elmegreen, B. G., Zimon, M. J., and Yeo, K. M. (IBM). Hyperuniform and nearly hyperuniform neural networks. US20240202508A1, published 2024-06-20.
sources.verification: Application text, inventor and publication metadata inspected; description explicitly mentions extending HU/NHU sparse topology to sparse self-attention in transformers (Google Patents displayed lines 205 and 444 at access time).
claims_supported: HU/NHU geometry-derived sparse feedforward networks have direct prior art.
The description expressly proposes extending this topology to sparse attention in transformers.
limitations: Patent examples are not independent peer-reviewed validation.
The text does not establish causal benefit of multicomponent MHU attention masks.
No inference concerning legal validity, infringement, patentability or freedom to operate is made.
sources.implementation_relevance: Do not claim that combining HU placement with sparse attention is the novel contribution; test a differentiable causal multicomponent hypothesis instead.

sources.citation: Di Giovanni, F., Giusti, L., Barbero, F., Luise, G., Lio, P., and Bronstein, M. M. (2023). On Over-Squashing in Message Passing Neural Networks: The Impact of Width, Depth, and Topology. ICML, PMLR 202:7865-7885.
sources.verification: Official ICML/PMLR bibliographic record and abstract opened.
claims_supported: Width, depth and topology jointly affect over-squashing and useful long-range sensitivity.
Hop accessibility alone is insufficient to establish effective message transmission.
limitations: Commute-time claims are not literal bounds for LARP's directed, nonlinear, normalized tied recurrence.
The paper supplies no MHU-specific benefit or XOR learning guarantee.
sources.implementation_relevance: Measure sensitivity, path multiplicities, state mixing and true computation instead of treating added layers as a mechanism by themselves.
